Bedkow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Gutków, Poland

Not demolished. This record contains a contradiction worth flagging: it is categorized as demolished, yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'no.' Będków's Jews, who first arrived in the 18th century to rent the local inn before departing and only returning in the 19th century, were subordinate to the Jewish community in Ujazd; the town's poor Jewish community worked mainly in small trade and crafts. Between April and September 1942, a ghetto here held about 300 people, including Jews from Będków, Rzgów, and Tuszyn, before their deportation to Treblinka. This cemetery, likely established in the 19th century, was mentioned in the press as early as 1876 in connection with a trial of three local inhabitants.
